Winners of the Forward Prizes for Poetry 2025
Posted 16 February 2026
At a packed ceremony in the Southbank Centre’s Queen Elizabeth Hall on Sunday evening, the winners of the 2025 Forward Prizes for Poetry were announced by host Joelle Taylor and chair of judges Sarah Hall.
Forward Prize for Best Collection Joint Winner 2025
Vidyan Ravinthiran
Avidya (Bloodaxe Books)
Written in the wake of co-editing Out of Sri Lanka , a landmark anthology of Sri Lankan and diasporic poetry, Avidya grew out of a deepened sense of cultural lineage and personal inheritance. The collection reflects on the experience of migration, of living across geographies and identities, and on the dislocation of moving, alongside his wife and son, from the UK to the US, just before the pandemic and its attendant travel bans.
Forward Prize for Best Collection Joint Winner 2025
Karen Solie
Wellwater (Picador)
In Wellwater , Solie returns to themes long central to her poetry, landscape, labour, and inequality but with a deepened emotional resonance. The collection charts how age, loss, and mourning alter not only the self but the very shape of language. As she notes, the line between elegy and ode is often barely there, and her poems move deftly between lament and praise, between clarity and ambiguity.
Jerwood Prize Best First Collection Winner 2025
Isabelle Baafi
Chaotic Good (Faber & Faber)
Chaotic Good is a powerful and searching debut that navigates the complexities of ambivalence, trauma, and transformation. At times dreamlike and at others razor-sharp, Baafi’s collection draws from the subconscious, from early-morning thoughts and fragments of memory to shape poems that feel both deeply intimate and universally resonant.
Forward Prize for Best Single Poem – Written Winner 2025
Abeer Ameer
‘At Least’ ( MODRON )
Drawing on real news reports, ‘at least’ is a searing meditation on violence, loss, and the language we use to describe tragedy. Through repetition and restraint, Ameer’s poem bears witness to lives lost and questions what it means to remember with care.
Forward Prize for Best Single Poem – Performed Winner 2025
Griot Gabriel
‘Where I’m From’
‘Where I’m From’ celebrates that Machester, particularly Longsight and Ardwick. ‘It highlights both the joys and sorrows of my community,’ he writes, ‘which seem to resonate deeply with people from various parts of the country – particularly those familiar with – yet proud of – the struggles from which they were birthed.’
